notes: CBSA's create-customer service (CRECUST) on GENERATED Db2 rows (#4507). CRECUST's only Db2 statement is INSERT INTO PROCTRAN: it reads no ACCOUNT, CUSTOMER or CONTROL row (CUSTOMER and its control record are VSAM, customer.txt), so there is nothing to prove on generated CONTROL or ACCOUNT rows; PROCTRAN (no key, no foreign key in CRETB02) starts with 12 generated rows (every column at its boundaries, a NULL in every nullable column) and is compared after every task with each task's statements (compare_sql). 16 generated LINKs with BNK1CCS's SUBPGM-PARMS: name and address lengths from 1 byte to the field's width, and only dates of birth BEFORE 1601, so each ends in DATE-OF-BIRTH-CHECK's refusal ('O') ahead of the CEEDAYS call after the five-child credit check. ASSUMED (register, as cbsa-crecust): L1 (CEEDAYS picture 10 over 8; the 2 slack bytes are ruled blank, owner 2026-10-23: a date of birth from 1601 on is modelled and stays in cbsa-crecust) and X18 (the child schedule is ASSUMED). These scenarios reach only the credit check and the refusal, a partial reach; no PROCTRAN row is inserted. Burned estate (CBSA). Data: customer.txt is cbsa-custctrl's, SYNTHETIC.
